message: docs(contract): ids is required, severity has no parameter, no raw literal remains

edits.find: Both are fixed where the rule is defined rather than restated by whoever reports it, and exactly one of the two is fully enforced today. `severity` **defaults** to the rule's own answer through `ruleSeverity`, rather than to the literal `"error"` it used to default to; the constructor's `severity` parameter still exists and a call site can still name one, so this is a corrected default rather than an invariant, and deleting the parameter is owed.
edits.replace: Both are fixed where the rule is defined rather than restated by whoever reports it, and both are fully enforced today. `severity` is derived through `ruleSeverity` and through nothing else: the constructor has no `severity` parameter, so there is no argument position in which a call site could name one, and this is an invariant rather than a corrected default.

edits.find: `ids` is optional in the type rather than always present, and that is a measured intermediate state rather than the destination: three raw producers still omit the member, and it becomes required in the slice that converts them. Every diagnostic built through the one constructor in `contract/diagnostics.ts` already carries it, frozen and empty for a rule that names none. See ADR-097.
edits.replace: `ids` is required in the type and always present, which is the destination the optional member was a measured step towards. Every diagnostic is built through the one constructor in `contract/diagnostics.ts` and carries it frozen, empty for a rule that names none. No producer omits the member, because no raw producer is left: the last four to hold a shape of their own, in `graph/order.ts`, `graph/references.ts` and `runtime/graph-publisher.ts`, forward through the constructor now. See ADR-097.

edits.find: Ownership is enforced where a diagnostic is built, as the argument list the rule derives, rather than by the shape of the field: `ids` stays optional on the type for now, and every diagnostic built through the one constructor carries it, frozen and empty for a rule that names none. `severity` is derived from the record by default, though the constructor still accepts one, so a rule's answer is the default rather than yet an invariant. See ADR-097.
edits.replace: Ownership is enforced where a diagnostic is built, as the argument list the rule derives, and the field agrees with it: `ids` is required on the type, and every diagnostic is built through the one constructor and carries it, frozen and empty for a rule that names none. `severity` is derived from the record by that same constructor, which takes no severity argument, so a rule's answer is an invariant rather than a default a caller could overrule. See ADR-097.

edits.find:
`severity` comes from the rule by default rather than from a fixed `"error"`. It used to default to `"error"` at the constructor, so a warning rule reported by a caller that passed nothing became an error diagnostic and nothing noticed; the rule answers instead. The constructor still takes a `severity` argument, so a caller that names one explicitly still overrides the rule, and a handful inside this project do. Read `severity` off the diagnostic and do not pass one.

Whether a rule names `ids` is fixed by the rule too, but it is enforced where a diagnostic is built rather than by the field. A producer takes the payload its rule owns as its argument list, so a rule that names none cannot be handed one and a rule that always names them cannot omit them. The field itself stays optional. Every diagnostic built through the project's one constructor carries it, frozen and empty for a rule that names none, so for those `ids` and `ids ?? []` read the same thing. Three producers inside the project still hand-build their object and omit the member, so keep spelling `ids ?? []` until the field is required.
edits.replace:
`severity` comes from the rule and from nowhere else. It used to default to `"error"` at the constructor, so a warning rule reported by a caller that passed nothing became an error diagnostic and nothing noticed. The constructor no longer takes a `severity` argument at all, so there is nothing to pass and nothing to override: read `severity` off the diagnostic.

Whether a rule names `ids` is fixed by the rule too, and it is enforced where a diagnostic is built, as the argument list the rule derives. A producer takes the payload its rule owns, so a rule that names none cannot be handed one and a rule that always names them cannot omit them. **The field is required, so read `ids` directly.** Every diagnostic carries it, frozen, and empty for a rule that names none, so `ids ?? []` is a guard against a case the type no longer has: drop it. Every producer inside the project forwards to the one constructor, and none hand-builds an object of its own.

edits.find: `severity` is derived from the same record, through `ruleSeverity`, which is now the constructor's default in place of the literal `"error"` it used to be.
edits.replace: `severity` is derived from the same record, through `ruleSeverity`, which is now the only expression in the tree that answers the question rather than the constructor's default.

edits.find: The parameter itself survives, and saying otherwise is the overclaim this record's own status paragraph exists to catch; it was said here once and is corrected in place rather than beside. A call site can still name a severity: `contract/validate-v5.ts` names one at several sites, `adapters/trigger-factory/default.ts` names one too, and `validate-v5.ts`'s own local helper still carries a `= "error"` default of its own one layer above, which is the same bug one level up and harmless today only because both keyframe warnings pass `"warning"` by hand. So this is a corrected default and not yet the invariant a reader might take it for. Deleting the parameter is owed, and what it is owed first is the compiler enumerating its call sites rather than a fourth hand count.
edits.replace: The parameter is deleted, and the two corrections this paragraph has carried are both recorded here in place rather than beside. It first claimed the invariant while only the default had moved, which is the overclaim this record's own status paragraph exists to catch; it then said the parameter survives, which was true when it was written. Neither is true now. Nineteen sites named a severity and every one of them named the severity its rule already fixes, so no diagnostic moved when the parameter went; the compiler enumerated those sites rather than a fourth hand count, which is what deleting it was owed. `contract/validate-v5.ts` forwards a rule id, a path and a message, its own local helper carries no `= "error"` default any more, and `adapters/trigger-factory/default.ts` names no severity. There is no argument position left in which a call site could name one, so this is the invariant a reader would take it for.

edits.find: The generic constructors are narrowed at the same time, and there are six rather than five. `contract/diagnostics.ts` `diagnostic`, `graph/ir.ts` `diag`, `runtime/report.ts` `frozenDiagnostic`, `domain/keyframe-compiler.ts` `diagnostic`, the plugin `diagnostic`, and `graph-runtime.ts` `#report` all take `string` today, and a closed union whose only producer accepts `string` is closed nowhere.
edits.replace: The generic constructors are narrowed at the same time, and there are six rather than five. `contract/diagnostics.ts` `diagnostic`, `graph/ir.ts` `diag`, `runtime/report.ts` `frozenDiagnostic`, `domain/keyframe-compiler.ts` `diagnostic`, the plugin `diagnostic`, and `graph-runtime.ts` `#report` took `string` before this record landed, and a closed union whose only producer accepts `string` is closed nowhere. All six take `RuleId` now, and the five that are not the constructor forward to it rather than building a frozen shape of their own, so the shape has one owner and the severity has one answer.

edits.find: There is no variant left to be checked against and no narrowing for an assertion to reach: with `Diagnostic` flat, `asDiagnostic` is a widening rather than a correlation stated once, so the "boundary stated rather than implied" this paragraph was written to describe stops describing a union. The widening survives only for the raw producers that still build a frozen object literal of their own, and it is deleted with the last of them. The assertion's own input is a separate question and the honest answer is that it is unchanged: `DiagnosticFields` keeps `ruleId` and `ids` independent, so a module calling `asDiagnostic` directly can still name a rule by a literal and hand over a payload it does not own. Three modules call it, all three are producers that derive their own list, and a fourth caller is the thing to refuse. This is therefore an assertion boundary rather than an invariant over every construction, and a record claiming otherwise would be the overclaim this paragraph exists to prevent.
edits.replace: There is no variant left to be checked against and no narrowing for an assertion to reach: with `Diagnostic` flat, `asDiagnostic` was a widening rather than a correlation stated once, so it was deleted with the last of the raw producers it survived for, and `DiagnosticFields` went with it. That closes the hole this paragraph used to name rather than merely bounding it: nothing can name a rule by a literal and hand over a payload it does not own, because there is no expression left that accepts the two independently. This is therefore an invariant over every construction rather than an assertion boundary, and it is stated only now that it is true.

edits.find: What the compiler still cannot answer for is a producer forwarding a rule id it holds as data: `contract/validate-v5.ts` through `scopedRuleId`, whose two scopes are both idless, and `runtime/report.ts` through the private `frozenDiagnostic`, which is reached only from the exported member that now derives its own list. Those two are the widening's whole remaining subject, and both are backed by the record in `contract/rule.ts` rather than by a proof.
edits.replace: Two producers forward a rule id they hold as data rather than as a literal, and neither is an open question any more. `contract/validate-v5.ts` reaches the constructor through `scopedRuleId`, whose return type is narrowed to `KeyframeRuleId | ContributionRuleId`; every member of both families owns no ids, so the derived list is the empty one and the forwarding call is checked against it rather than accepted by a branch with no claim in it. `runtime/report.ts` reaches it through the private `frozenDiagnostic`, which is reached only from the exported member that derives its own list. The first is backed by the compiler and the second by the record in `contract/rule.ts`.

edits.find: `graph/ir.ts`'s `diag`, which held a hardcoded `severity: "error"` and a conditional `ids` spread, was collapsed into the one constructor, while the equivalent producers in `runtime/report.ts`, `domain/plugins.ts` and `domain/keyframe-compiler.ts` still hold both and are owed the same collapse, and `contract/diagnostic-ids.ts` was deleted.
edits.replace: `graph/ir.ts`'s `diag`, which held a hardcoded `severity: "error"` and a conditional `ids` spread, was collapsed into the one constructor, the equivalent producers in `runtime/report.ts`, `domain/plugins.ts` and `domain/keyframe-compiler.ts` were collapsed after it, the four raw object literals in `graph/order.ts`, `graph/references.ts` and `runtime/graph-publisher.ts` were the last of the second ownership and forward through the constructor now, the `severity` parameter itself was deleted, and `contract/diagnostic-ids.ts` was deleted. One further correctness question fell out of the ownership record rather than out of the rename: both deferred rules in `runtime/report.ts` answer `ids: "always"`, and `OwnedIds` proves that an argument was passed and never that it says anything, so a deferral was able to publish a warning whose payload named nothing. `DeferredSeeds` requires a seed list with at least one member, which makes that unrepresentable rather than merely unreached.

edits.find: The six generic constructors take `RuleId` where they took `string`, `validateKeyframes` takes one `scope` where it took a prefix, an alias map and a group flag, and `Diagnostic.ruleId` is `RuleId`, which is the public surface change: a consumer constructing a `Diagnostic` with a rule id of its own invention stops compiling. `contract/rule.ts` owns what each rule is, checked total against that enumeration by `satisfies`, and `Diagnostic` is flat again: `severity` derives from the rule and `ids` is required and empty for a rule that names none, so `asDiagnostic`, `DiagnosticFields` and `contract/diagnostic-ids.ts` are deleted rather than re-justified. One constructor builds every diagnostic and the five producers forward to it; four raw literals in `graph/` and the constructor's own `severity` parameter, which thirteen sites still pass, are what remain owed. Green on `0931c0a` at all seven jobs; it is not merged, and the runs that measured it belong to that pull request.
edits.replace: The six generic constructors take `RuleId` where they took `string`, `validateKeyframes` takes one `scope` where it took a prefix, an alias map and a group flag, and `Diagnostic.ruleId` is `RuleId`, which is the public surface change: a consumer constructing a `Diagnostic` with a rule id of its own invention stops compiling. `contract/rule.ts` owns what each rule is, checked total against that enumeration by `satisfies`, and `Diagnostic` is flat again: `severity` derives from the rule and `ids` is required and empty for a rule that names none, so `asDiagnostic`, `DiagnosticFields` and `contract/diagnostic-ids.ts` are deleted rather than re-justified. One constructor builds every diagnostic and every producer forwards to it: the `severity` parameter is deleted, so no call site can name one; the last four raw literals in `graph/order.ts`, `graph/references.ts` and `runtime/graph-publisher.ts` are collapsed, so none remain; `scopedRuleId` is narrowed to `KeyframeRuleId | ContributionRuleId`, so the validator's forwarding call is checked against the empty list rather than accepted by a branch with no claim in it; and a deferred batch takes a non-empty `DeferredSeeds`, so a rule that always names ids can no longer publish a payload naming nothing. Green on `b8f9436c5b761b545190ece07d411697892de2ad` at all seven jobs, run `35439056329`. What remains is the pull request body and an independent quality pass; it is not merged, it is still a draft on `feat/449-rule-id-closed-union` rather than on `main`, and the runs that measured it belong to that pull request.
